reply_text:
I found two 2011 predictions by Demis Hassabis. Both are already on your recorded list, and I found nothing new.

**Where they come from:** Hassabis gave a talk called "Combining Systems Neuroscience and Machine Learning to Build AGI" at the Future of Humanity Institute's Winter Intelligence Conference in Oxford. The conference's own schedule page puts it on Sunday 16 January 2011, 15:30–16:30.

**How strong the source is:** The YouTube recording (uploaded 12 Dec 2011, which is probably why some sites call it a "Dec 2011" talk) wouldn't play past a bot-protection page, so I never heard his actual words. The quotes below come from Tom Rochette's blog. He says the page holds "most of the content of the slides". That makes it a third-party summary of the slides, not a transcript, so I marked it coverage_only. Someone needs to watch the video to confirm his exact wording.

**What the slides predict:**
- Systems that can carry learning over to new tasks and pick up concepts will appear "in the next 5 years".
- Full human-level AGI is "Probably ~20+ years" away.

**Other searching:**
- One page summarising the talk (whatishappening.org) was blocked, so I didn't quote it.
- A search for the AGI-11 conference (August 2011, Google) found no talk by Hassabis.
- An Internet Archive recording on neuroscience turned out to be from the 2010 Singularity Summit, so it's listed under other_years.
- I used 7 of 12 searches and 5 of 6 page openings.
